result:
The top bar now stays fixed on every page, and clicking Calendar or the app title while you're already on the calendar does nothing. I tested this in a real browser on a copy of your data, at five screen sizes from 1300px down to 320px wide, and the two general test suites still pass. Your real database's fingerprint stayed the same, and nothing is committed.

**Restart the app to see this**, since the shared page template changed, then hard-refresh once (Cmd+Shift+R) to load the new styles.

- **On the calendar:** neither one has a link there, so a click can't reload or move anything. The test confirmed no page request and the same scroll position. Calendar still looks like the other links but isn't clickable. This also applies on the "create a plan" page, because it's what the calendar shows when you have no plan.
- **From any other page:** Calendar and the title do the same thing and land on the current week, with the top bar and the "This week" toolbar visible and the week's header right below them.
- **Top bar:** it stayed at the very top on the calendar, Plans, Profile, the plan form and the summary, including at the bottom of a long plan. The "This week" toolbar now pins directly under it, so both stay visible while you scroll.
- **"This week" button:** it still jumps back to the current week.

**Phone-sized screens needed two extra changes** (700px wide or less), because a fixed bar that wrapped onto several lines would have taken up too much of the screen:
- The title sits on one row and the links on the row below.
- A long title or username is cut off with "…". On the narrowest screens you'll see "Build 1 (feature-…" and "ui_test_u…".

This also removed the small sideways scroll at 320px wide that I mentioned last time. Long usernames are also cut off on desktop, past about 10rem.

The login and signup templates are unchanged, and the title there is still plain text. Those pages do share the top bar's styling, so the bar is now fixed there too, with a very similar height.
